commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

# Start here

Every agent doc for this repo lives in `.agents/`. The root `AGENTS.md` and
`CLAUDE.md` only point here. This file is the operating contract for **any**
agent or engineer: concrete commands, explicit rules, no tribal knowledge. When
the way we work changes, change it here.

## What this repo is

A reference scaffold for **agentic engineering**: the files, gates, and context
that make AI-written code consistent and enterprise-grade. TypeScript + React is
just the runnable carrier. The scaffolding is the point (see the root
`README.md` and [`NORTH_STAR.md`](NORTH_STAR.md)).

## Run it

```bash
pnpm install          # install dependencies (Node ≥ 22.18, pnpm)
pnpm setup:agents     # install the external agentic toolkit (one time)
pnpm dev              # run web (http://localhost:5173) and api (:3001) together; Vite proxies /trpc
pnpm lint:policy      # ESLint: policy, React hooks, and React Compiler rules
pnpm arch:check       # architecture gate, structure check, diagram freshness, API report freshness
pnpm arch:diagram     # regenerate docs/architecture/roles.mmd and each result's architecture.mmd
pnpm api:report       # regenerate each package's etc/*.api.md after an intended export change
pnpm verify           # the full local gate suite (typecheck → biome → eslint → react doctor → fallow → architecture → tests → build)
pnpm e2e              # playwright test: every spec in each result's web/e2e/, with its api and web servers
```

## Run a Todo trial

The orchestrator runs each Todo trial; an agent inside a trial builds its
result from the prompt alone. Run trials one at a time, from the checkout
that keeps the evidence, at the scaffold revision every trial shares
([ADR 0034](decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)):

```bash
pnpm trial --trial 1 --scaffold <rev> --trials-root <dir> --dry-run   # print the plan and the exact claude argv
pnpm trial --trial 1 --scaffold <rev> --trials-root <dir>             # clone, run one fresh session, check, record
git fetch <dir>/todo-01-<stamp>/repo trial/todo-01:trial/todo-01         # keep the result branch
```

The run writes `docs/trials/todo-01.json`, the agent's stream as
`todo-01.stream.jsonl` with secrets redacted (and `todo-01.patch` when it
fails), and prints its workdir. Fetch the result branch, then remove the
workdir before the next trial; the harness refuses to start while one
remains. Pass `--retry` only after a failure from before the agent started.

## The golden rules

1. **Read before you write.** Architecture, conventions, the Definition of Done,
   the glossary, and ADRs live in this folder.
2. **Follow the patterns; copy the templates.** New files come from
   [`templates/`](templates/). Consistency is the deliverable.
3. **Behaviour is defined by the E2E map**, each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`
   (for example `apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`), not by the implementation.
   Add behaviour there first.
4. **When a gate fails, fix the cause.** Keep every gate and its config as it
   is; the checks below enforce this.
5. **Done means the gates are green.** Report a task complete once
   `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass; see
   [`project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md`](project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md).
6. **PRs carry proof.** Complete the pull request template and follow
   [`project/PR_QUALITY.md`](project/PR_QUALITY.md) before opening a PR or
   marking it ready.
7. **Change rules in the open.** When a constraint is wrong, propose an ADR in
   [`decisions/`](decisions/) and change the rule there.

## Rules and what enforces them

Each rule below fails a check when it is broken, so the check's message is the
first place to look. [`project/CONVENTIONS.md`](project/CONVENTIONS.md) lists
the code-level rules and their checks.

| Rule | Enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| Every file has one architecture role, and imports follow the role table and the contract in [`project/ARCHITECTURE.md`](project/ARCHITECTURE.md). | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`, `pnpm typecheck` |
| Commits, PR titles, and branch names follow Conventional Commits. | commitlint on `commit-msg`; `PR quality` workflow |
| Every hook runs; `--no-verify`, `git commit -n`, `HUSKY=0`, and `core.hooksPath`, alias, or config-include overrides are refused. | `.claude/hooks/block-gate-bypass.sh` (Claude Code, [ADR 0027](decisions/0027-block-common-hook-bypasses.md)); CI re-runs every gate |
| A change that loosens or rewrites a gate (`.husky/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `eslint.config.js`, `biome.json`, `commitlint.config.ts`, `tooling/eslint-plugin-policy.js`, `scripts/check-suppressions.mjs`) waits for BenSheridanEdwards to tick the sign-off for its head commit. A tick counts when it is made as BenSheridanEdwards. | `enforcement-approval` status ([ADR 0023](decisions/0023-protect-only-the-files-that-run-the-gates.md), [ADR 0024](decisions/0024-sign-off-only-loosening-enforcement-changes.md)) |
| Done means every gate is green on the latest commit. | `Required gates` and the checks in `docs/required-gates.md` |
| A PR body keeps the template sections and carries inline proof. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
| A new dependency arrives with an ADR. | `pnpm check:adr` |
| Secrets stay out of commits. | gitleaks in pre-commit and CI |
| Every lint or type suppression names its rule and its reason. | `pnpm check:suppressions`; Biome for `biome-ignore` |
| Generated files match their source. | `pnpm arch:check`, `pnpm gates:check`, `pnpm api:check` |
| Guidance docs state rules as the action to take. | `pnpm check:docs` |
| A doc that ties sign-off to a file names only a file the enforcement gate guards. | `pnpm check:docs` ([ADR 0030](decisions/0030-docs-name-only-guarded-paths-for-sign-off.md)) |

## Simplicity Mode

Use Ponytail for coding, review, refactor, and design tasks unless the user says
otherwise. Default level: `full`: delete code, reuse existing patterns, and use
stdlib or native platform features before adding abstractions or dependencies.

## What is here, and when to read it

| Path | Read it when… |
| --- | --- |
| [`project/AGENTIC_INFRASTRUCTURE.md`](project/AGENTIC_INFRASTRUCTURE.md) | …before changing agent guidance, hooks, workflows, or skills. |
| [`project/ARCHITECTURE.md`](project/ARCHITECTURE.md) | …before adding or moving any module: the role table, the api file roles, the state model, and how to add a route, a feature or a procedure. It is the pattern you must follow. |
| [`project/CONVENTIONS.md`](project/CONVENTIONS.md) | …while writing code: naming, structure, imports, errors, state. |
| [`project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md`](project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md) | …before you claim a task is finished. The gates enforce this list. |
| [`project/QUALITY_GATES.md`](project/QUALITY_GATES.md) | …before changing hooks, scripts, CI, or tool ownership. |
| [`project/PR_QUALITY.md`](project/PR_QUALITY.md) | …before opening, updating, or marking a pull request ready. |
| [`project/TECH_STACK.md`](project/TECH_STACK.md) | …to know which tool owns which concern (and what *not* to add). |
| [`project/GLOSSARY.md`](project/GLOSSARY.md) | …when you meet a domain term. Use these words exactly, in code and prose. |
| [`decisions/`](decisions/) | …to understand *why* a constraint exists before you challenge it. ADRs. |
| [`templates/`](templates/) | …when creating a new component, test, or E2E flow. Copy from here. |
| [`NORTH_STAR.md`](NORTH_STAR.md) | …to see where the repo is heading and why. |
| [`PROGRESS.md`](PROGRESS.md) | …when picking up multi-step work, or to checkpoint a task longer than three steps. |
| [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) | …to find handed-off work and its acceptance criteria. |
| [`CLAUDE_CODE.md`](CLAUDE_CODE.md) | …if you are Claude Code: skills, settings, hooks, and tooling. |
| [`GITNEXUS.md`](GITNEXUS.md) | …before editing a symbol: impact analysis and change detection. |
| [`openai.yaml`](openai.yaml) | …if you are an OpenAI-family agent: the same entry points as a manifest. |
| [`verify-agentic-template`](../.claude/skills/verify-agentic-template/SKILL.md) | …to drive the app and capture PR proof. |

## Safety

- Keep secrets out of commits; CI runs a secret scan and a dependency audit.
- Keep one owner per concern: Biome formats and runs general lint, ESLint runs
  policy and React rules, Jest and Playwright run tests. A new tool for an owned
  concern needs an ADR (see [`project/TECH_STACK.md`](project/TECH_STACK.md));
  `pnpm check:adr` fails a new dependency that no new ADR names.
- Treat generated artefacts (`apps/web/dist/`, `.cache/`, `coverage/`, `graphify-out/`,
  `.gitnexus/`) as disposable; regenerate them with their command.

# Architecture

> This is the anchor for **showcase #2**: agent-written code must follow the
> patterns described here. When asked to verify or review work, an agent checks
> the change against this document first.

## The shape

The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):

- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference
  result lives in `apps/` (`@repo/web`, `@repo/api`). Each generated trial
  result lives in `showcase/<id>/` with the same shape.
- `packages/ui` (`@repo/ui`) holds the UI primitives every result renders with.
- `tooling/results.mjs` (`listResults`) is the one place that discovers
  results: the reference first, then each `showcase/<id>` that has both
  `web/package.json` and `api/package.json`, sorted by id.

The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
joins every gate with no config entry of its own.

The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.

```
apps/
├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider
│   │   ├── App.tsx                      # mounts the routes; holds no business logic
│   │   ├── index.css
│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient
│   │   │   ├── TestApiProvider.tsx      # the same providers over typed in-memory handlers

## Roles

[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any import the table does not allow, and
`coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. Paths
below are relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).

| Role | Files | May import | Type-only import |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` | |
| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role | `api-app` |
| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` | |
| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` | |
| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role | |
| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` | |
| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role | |
| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` | `api-domain` |
| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` | |
| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role | |
| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` | |

Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
role.

The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
shows every role and every direction the rules allow, dashed where only a
type-only import is allowed. Each result has its own generated diagram,
[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
resolve to. Both come from `pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.

## Result structure

`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):

- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
  role.
- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
  rather than link it.
- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
  lists only external ones.
- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
  pragma.

## The api file roles

| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. Application calls it. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |

The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:

```ts
// apps/api/src/router.ts
import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
import { router } from './trpc.ts';

export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
```

Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
because Vite resolves it.

## The web state model

| State | Owner | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: effectTsResolver(schema), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
mutation or form of its own.

The api client is the only web module that names the api. Everything else
reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:

```ts
// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
const trpc = useTrpc();
const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));

// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const mutation = useMutation(
  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
  }),
);
```

Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:

```tsx
function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
  const view = render(
    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
      <GreetingPage />
    </TestApiProvider>,
  );
  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
}
```

A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

`contract/<id>` is a rule in
[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc),
which Fallow loads as a rule pack and reports as an error. The behaviour map
is each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, for example
[`apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`](../../apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts); see
[ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-behaviour-mapped-with-e2e.md).

## Architecture checks

`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
file:

- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
  differs from a fresh run.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.

`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
included.

## Showcase results

A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.

- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
  nothing from another result.
- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.

## What this template intentionally omits

The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.

## How to extend

Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.

### Add an api feature

1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
   storage or any effect.
2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.

### Add a procedure

1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
   `.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(schema))`.
2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
   delegate to one application function.
3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
   `procedures.test.ts`.

### Add a route

1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
   `index.ts` that exports the page.
2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
   runs every spec in that folder.

### Add a web feature

Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
import it through its `index.ts`.

### Finish

1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

| State | Owner | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` from the api client, with `queryOptions` or `mutationOptions` | `use<Name>.ts` in the route folder (`useGreeting.ts`) |

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |

## Judgment calls

- **Full words in identifiers.** Write `name` and `request`. The name is the
  cheapest documentation an agent has. Established acronyms such as E2E, CI,
  ADR, UI, IO, and URL are fine.
- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See
  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.
- **Validate data at an IO boundary.** Parse network, storage, and environment
  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect
  Schema. A type assertion is a claim, and validation is proof.
- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.
- **Co-locate tests.** Each test sits beside its subject as `<Name>.test.ts(x)`.

254	  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
255	- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
256	  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
257	  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
258	  differs from a fresh run.
259	- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
260	  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
261	  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
262	  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
263	  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
264	  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.
265	
266	`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
267	point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
268	with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
269	included.
270	
271	## Showcase results
272	
273	A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
274	([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
275	harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
276	lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.
277	
278	- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
279	  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
280	- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
281	  nothing from another result.
282	- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
283	  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
284	- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
285	  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
286	- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
287	  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
288	
289	## What this template intentionally omits
290	
291	The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
292	are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
293	inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
294	in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.
295	
296	## How to extend
297	
298	Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
299	reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.
300	
301	### Add an api feature
302	
303	1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
304	   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
305	   storage or any effect.
306	2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
307	   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
308	   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
309	3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
310	   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.
311	
312	### Add a procedure
313	
314	1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
315	   `.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(schema))`.
316	2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
317	   delegate to one application function.
318	3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
319	   `procedures.test.ts`.
320	
321	### Add a route
322	
323	1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
324	   `index.ts` that exports the page.
325	2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
326	   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
327	   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
328	3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
329	4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
330	5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
331	   runs every spec in that folder.
332	
333	### Add a web feature
334	
335	Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
336	is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
337	import it through its `index.ts`.
338	
339	### Finish
340	
341	1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
342	2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
343	   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
344	3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.
345	# Conventions
346	
347	Each convention below names the check that enforces it. The error message of
348	each check names the fix. The judgment calls at the end are the conventions no
349	check can decide; reviewers hold those. When in doubt, copy the reference
350	feature.
351	
352	## Enforced conventions
353	
354	The ESLint rules and the Biome naming override run on every package source:
355	`{apps,packages}/*/src/**` and `showcase/*/*/src/**`.
356	
357	| Convention | Enforced by |
358	| --- | --- |
359	| Folders under a package `src/` are kebab-case (`name-input`). | ESLint `policy/folder-names` |
360	| Identifiers: `camelCase` functions and variables, `PascalCase` types and components, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for true configuration constants. | Biome `style/useNamingConvention` |
361	| File names are camelCase, PascalCase, or the name of their export. | Biome `style/useFilenamingConvention` |
362	| A component or hook lives in the file of the same name (`GreetingForm.tsx`, `useGreeting.ts`). | ESLint `policy/file-matches-export` |
363	| One React component per file. | ESLint `policy/one-component-per-file` |
364	| Function components only. | ESLint `react-doctor/prefer-function-component` |
365	| `useState`, `useReducer`, effects, TanStack Query hooks (`useQuery`, `useSuspenseQuery`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `useMutation`) and React Hook Form hooks (`useForm`, `useFieldArray`) run only inside a named custom `use*` hook. | ESLint `policy/state-and-effects-in-hooks` ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-local-state-inside-custom-hooks.md)) |
366	| `useForm` takes `resolver: effectTsResolver(schema)` from `@hookform/resolvers/effect-ts`. | ESLint `policy/form-uses-effect-schema` |
367	| Every api procedure input is `.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(schema))` with `Schema` from `effect`. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` |
368	| Derived values are computed during render instead of copied into state by an effect. | ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, `react-doctor/no-derived-state`, `react-doctor/no-mirror-prop-effect` |
369	| Functions defined inside a component start with `handle` (`handleGreet`). | ESLint `policy/handler-names` |
370	| Callback props start with `on` (`onGreet`). | ESLint `policy/callback-prop-names` |
371	| Page components (`<Name>Page`) live in `src/routes/<route-name>/`. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` zone |
372	| Each file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` sits in a slice folder, and a slice imports no sibling slice. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation`, Fallow child zones for `apps/web` |
373	| A relative import stays inside its package; other packages are imported by name (`@repo/ui`). | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` |
374	| Another module imports a route, feature or api feature only through its `index.ts`: `./routes/greeting` in the web, `./features/greeting/index.ts` in the api. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports` |
375	| Every relative import in an api package names its `.ts` extension (`./application.ts`). | `pnpm typecheck` (`tsconfig.api.json`, `NodeNext`) and Node at runtime |
376	| Api code uses only erasable TypeScript syntax and sees no DOM; web code has the DOM and no Node globals. | `pnpm typecheck` (`tsconfig.api.json` with `erasableSyntaxOnly`; `tsconfig.json` with the DOM libs and no Node types) |
377	| Every source file belongs to one architecture role. | Fallow `coverage.requireAllFiles` (`pnpm arch:gate`) |
378	| Imports follow the role table in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md). | Fallow boundaries (`pnpm arch:gate`) |
379	| Banned imports, calls and effects per role. | Fallow rule pack, reported as `contract/<id>` (`pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`) |
380	| `strict` TypeScript with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `noUnusedLocals`. | `pnpm typecheck`; review of the diff catches a loosened `tsconfig.base.json` ([ADR 0023](../decisions/0023-protect-only-the-files-that-run-the-gates.md)) |
381	| `unknown` and narrowing in place of `any`. | Biome `suspicious/noExplicitAny` |
382	| `import type` for type-only imports. | Biome `style/useImportType`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` |
383	| `interface` for object shapes, `type` for unions and aliases. | Biome `style/useConsistentTypeDefinitions` |
384	| Import order. | Biome `organizeImports` |
385	| Every block has a body; a handled error does something observable. | Biome `suspicious/noEmptyBlockStatements` |
386	| Every lint or type suppression names its rule and carries its reason. | `pnpm check:suppressions`; Biome for `biome-ignore` |
387	| Every `fallow-ignore` comment names its reason. | Fallow `require-suppression-reason` |
388	| Accessible, labelled controls and status regions. | Biome `a11y/*`, jest-axe, `@axe-core/playwright`, Lighthouse |
389	
390	## Contract rules
391	
392	The Fallow rule pack
393	[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc)
394	reports each finding as `policy-violation` `contract/<id>`, an error. Tests are
395	outside every rule.
396	
397	| Rule id | What it keeps |
398	| --- | --- |
399	| `contract/domain-pure` | `domain.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`, no `effect` and no Node module. `tsconfig.domain.json` also gives it no Node globals. |
400	| `contract/application-without-trpc` | `application.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`; procedures map errors to tRPC. |
401	| `contract/effects-in-integrations` | `fetch`, `self.fetch`, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync` and `Effect.runFork` run only in `integrations.ts` or the api `server.ts` and `router.ts`. |
402	| `contract/io-effects-in-integrations` | Network, storage, process and shell work runs only there too. |
403	| `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | Node IO modules (`fs`, `http`, `net`, `child_process`) are imported only there too. |
404	| `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client` | `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query` are imported only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
405	| `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | Web and ui code imports `@trpc/server` only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
406	| `contract/ui-without-logic` | `packages/ui` imports no query, form, schema or tRPC library. |
407	
408	## State ownership
409	
410	| State | Owner | File |
411	| --- | --- | --- |
412	| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` from the api client, with `queryOptions` or `mutationOptions` | `use<Name>.ts` in the route folder (`useGreeting.ts`) |
413	| Form state | React Hook Form with `effectTsResolver(schema)` and `defaultValues` | `use<Name>Form.ts` (`useGreetingForm.ts`) |
414	| Form schema | Effect Schema | `<name>FormSchema.ts` (`greetingFormSchema.ts`) |
415	| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |
416	
417	After a mutation, refresh the queries it changes in `onSuccess` with
418	`queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() })`.
419	
420	## Api file roles
421	
422	| File | Holds |
423	| --- | --- |
424	| `features/<name>/procedures.ts` | The feature router. Validates each input with `Schema.standardSchemaV1` and delegates to application. |
425	| `features/<name>/application.ts` | Use cases. Calls domain and integrations; knows no transport. |
426	| `features/<name>/domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. |
427	| `features/<name>/integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect. |
428	| `features/<name>/index.ts` | The public surface: the feature router. |
429	
430	See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full role table and the
431	greeting reference.
432	
433	## Judgment calls
434	
435	- **Full words in identifiers.** Write `name` and `request`. The name is the
436	  cheapest documentation an agent has. Established acronyms such as E2E, CI,
437	  ADR, UI, IO, and URL are fine.
438	- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See
439	  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).
440	- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
441	  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.
442	- **Validate data at an IO boundary.** Parse network, storage, and environment
443	  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect
444	  Schema. A type assertion is a claim, and validation is proof.
445	- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.
446	- **Co-locate tests.** Each test sits beside its subject as `<Name>.test.ts(x)`.
447	
448	## Enforced commit and branch conventions
449	
450	| Convention | Enforced by |
451	| --- | --- |
452	| Commits use Conventional Commits, `type(scope): subject`, lower case with no trailing period. | commitlint on `commit-msg` |
453	| PR titles use Conventional Commits. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
454	| Branches are `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`, for example `feat/greeting-trim-name`. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
455	| A new dependency arrives with a new ADR that names it. | `pnpm check:adr` in `pnpm verify` and CI |
456	
457	## Commit judgment
458	
459	- Write the subject in the imperative mood.
460	- Keep one logical change per commit, so the diff stays reviewable.
461	# Definition of Done
462	
463	A change is **done** when every box below is true. This is not aspirational —
464	the quality gates mechanically enforce most of it, so "done" and "passes the
465	gates" are the same statement. A task is not done until the changed behaviour is
466	verified by deterministic evidence: tests, build output, typecheck and lint
467	results, screenshots or video for user-visible behaviour, or another concrete
468	artifact that stands without anyone's judgment. An agent reports a task
469	complete once `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` are green.
470	
471	## The checklist
472	
473	- [ ] **Behaviour is specified.** New or changed behaviour is covered by a
474	      spec in the result's `web/e2e/` folder (the behaviour map), such as
475	      `apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`. The product's contract is explicit.
476	- [ ] **Logic is unit-tested.** Domain, application and procedures have `api`
477	      Jest tests; hooks and pages have `web` Jest tests that render through
478	      `TestApiProvider`. Coverage stays at/above the threshold in
479	      `jest.config.ts` (80%).
480	- [ ] **Types check.** `pnpm typecheck` passes its four programs,
481	      `tsconfig.json` (web and ui), `tsconfig.node.json` (configs and e2e),
482	      `tsconfig.api.json` (api) and `tsconfig.domain.json` (api domain, no
483	      Node), with no `any` and no weakened config.
484	- [ ] **Lint + format clean.** `pnpm check` (Biome), `pnpm lint:policy`
485	      (ESLint), and `pnpm react-doctor` pass; every disabled rule carries a
486	      written reason.
487	- [ ] **Code intelligence clean.** `pnpm fallow:audit` reports no dead code,
488	      circular dependency, complexity, architecture or `contract/<id>` finding
489	      in any file the change touches.
490	- [ ] **Architecture checks pass.** `pnpm arch:check` passes: every file sits
491	      in a role, no forbidden import, every result passes the structure check,
492	      `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` and each result's `architecture.mmd` match
493	      `pnpm arch:diagram`, and every package's `etc/*.api.md` matches the code
494	      (`pnpm api:report` after an intended export change).
495	- [ ] **Build succeeds.** `pnpm build` produces a clean production bundle.
496	- [ ] **Accessible.** No axe violations (jest-axe in unit tests, `@axe-core/playwright`
497	      in the E2E run); interactive elements are reachable and labelled.
498	- [ ] **Within budget.** `pnpm size` passes (the bundle stays under the
499	      `.size-limit.json` budget).
500	- [ ] **PR proof is ready.** The pull request body follows
501	      [`PR_QUALITY.md`](PR_QUALITY.md) and the
502	      [pull request template](../../.github/pull_request_template.md), with exact
503	      local commands, visual proof or `Not applicable` with a reason, CI status,
504	      risk, rollback, and no private details.
505	- [ ] **Patterns followed.** The change matches
506	      [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [`CONVENTIONS.md`](CONVENTIONS.md);
507	      new files were created from [`../templates/`](../templates).
508	- [ ] **Decisions recorded.** Any new architectural choice is captured as an ADR
509	      in [`../decisions/`](../decisions). `pnpm check:adr` fails a change that
510	      adds a dependency unless an ADR added in the same change names it.
511	- [ ] **Commit is conventional.** Message follows Conventional Commits.
512	
513	## The one-command proof
514	
515	```bash
516	pnpm verify   # typecheck → biome → eslint → fallow → architecture → unit tests → build → size
517	pnpm e2e      # every result's behaviour map + axe accessibility scan
518	```
519	
520	If both are green and the checklist holds, the work is done. If either is red,
521	it is not — regardless of how finished the code looks.
522	
523	## PR contract checks
524	
525	The `PR quality` workflow runs
526	[`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`](../../scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs) on every
527	pull request event, including edits to the body. It fails the PR with a message
528	that names the fix unless:
529	
530	- the body keeps the four [template](../../.github/pull_request_template.md)
531	  sections in order, each with real content: `Why does this feature exist?`,
532	  `What changed?`, `Behavioural Proof (with video and screenshots)`, and
533	  `Verification Summary`;
534	- the proof section embeds a screenshot inline with `![alt](url)`, or says
535	  `Not applicable` followed by the technical reason on the same line or the
536	  next one;
537	- every inline image is an absolute `https://` URL, and a GitHub blob URL ends
538	  in `?raw=1`, so the image renders;
539	- the proof section embeds its images instead of linking to them;
540	- the title is Conventional Commits, `type(scope): summary`, with no agent or
541	  tool prefix;
542	- the head branch is `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`;
543	- the Verification Summary has exactly one `- Head commit:` line naming one SHA
544	  (full or short) of the PR head, so a push that moves the head fails until the
545	  body is re-checked against it
546	  ([ADR 0029](../decisions/0029-pr-body-names-its-head-commit.md)).
547	
548	## Proof judgment
549	
550	These calls need a reviewer:
551	
552	- Screenshots and video come from the branch under review and show the changed
553	  behaviour itself. Flows with motion or timing include video when practical.
554	- E2E tests map to the user-visible behaviour the PR changes.
555	- Every bug fix ships, in the same change, with the test that would have caught
556	  it. The test fails on the unfixed code and asserts the user-visible symptom.
557	- Missing visual proof or E2E coverage comes with a technical reason and the
558	  replacement verification method.
559	- Proof files live under `docs/proof/<short-scope>/` on the PR branch, unless
560	  the PR states a technical reason for another committed location. See
561	  [`.claude/skills/pr-inline-screenshot-proof/SKILL.md`](../../.claude/skills/pr-inline-screenshot-proof/SKILL.md).
562	- Each evidence link opens the rendered artifact once the branch is pushed.
563	
564	## Verification
565	
566	- Format, lint, typecheck, unit, integration, and E2E checks relevant to the
567	  changed files run after the final code change.
568	- The PR lists each command and its pass or fail result.
569	- The PR separates existing unrelated failures from failures it introduces.
570	- Each skipped check names its reason, risk, and follow-up owner.

# Architecture

> This is the anchor for **showcase #2**: agent-written code must follow the
> patterns described here. When asked to verify or review work, an agent checks
> the change against this document first.

## The shape

The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):

- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference
  result lives in `apps/` (`@repo/web`, `@repo/api`). Each generated trial
  result lives in `showcase/<id>/` with the same shape.
- `packages/ui` (`@repo/ui`) holds the UI primitives every result renders with.
- `tooling/results.mjs` (`listResults`) is the one place that discovers
  results: the reference first, then each `showcase/<id>` that has both
  `web/package.json` and `api/package.json`, sorted by id.

The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
joins every gate with no config entry of its own.

The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.

```
apps/
├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider
│   │   ├── App.tsx                      # mounts the routes; holds no business logic
│   │   ├── index.css
│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient
│   │   │   ├── TestApiProvider.tsx      # the same providers over typed in-memory handlers
│   │   │   ├── testApiHandlers.ts       # TestApiHandlers, one handler per procedure path
│   │   │   ├── useTestApiClients.ts
│   │   │   └── index.ts                 # public surface
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   │   └── greeting/                # one folder per route, kebab-case
│   │   │       ├── GreetingPage.tsx     # the page: composes the route's components
│   │   │       ├── GreetingForm.tsx     # one component per file
│   │   │       ├── GreetingMessage.tsx
│   │   │       ├── useGreeting.ts       # server state + local state
│   │   │       ├── useGreetingForm.ts   # form state
│   │   │       ├── greetingFormSchema.ts  # Effect Schema for the form
│   │   │       ├── *.test.ts(x)         # co-located tests
│   │   │       └── index.ts             # public surface: GreetingPage
│   │   └── features/<feature-name>/     # optional: web code that routes share
│   ├── e2e/                             # the behaviour map: greeting.spec.ts, accessibility.spec.ts
│   ├── etc/                             # generated API reports
│   └── vite.config.ts                   # proxies /trpc to API_ORIGIN (default http://127.0.0.1:3001)
└── api/                                 # @repo/api, Node with native type stripping
    ├── src/
    │   ├── server.ts                    # composition root: the HTTP server on PORT (default 3001)
    │   ├── router.ts                    # appRouter and the AppRouter type
    │   ├── trpc.ts                      # initTRPC: router, procedure, createCallerFactory
    │   └── features/
    │       └── greeting/
    │           ├── index.ts             # public surface: greetingRouter
    │           ├── procedures.ts        # validates input, delegates to application
    │           ├── application.ts       # use cases: greet
    │           ├── domain.ts            # pure types and rules: Greeting, formatGreeting
    │           ├── integrations.ts      # storage and every effect (the greeting has none)
    │           └── *.test.ts
    ├── etc/
    └── package.json                     # exports only { ".": { "types": "./src/router.ts" } }
packages/ui/                             # @repo/ui, react as its only peer
├── src/
│   ├── Button.tsx
│   ├── TextField.tsx
│   ├── styles.css                       # imported once in main.tsx as '@repo/ui/styles.css'
│   └── index.ts
└── etc/ui.api.md
showcase/<id>/                           # a Todo trial result: the same shape, scope @<id>
├── architecture.mmd                     # generated by pnpm arch:diagram
├── web/                                 # @<id>/web: package.json, index.html, vite.config.ts, src/, e2e/, etc/
└── api/                                 # @<id>/api: package.json, src/, etc/
```

## Roles

[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any import the table does not allow, and
`coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. Paths
below are relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).

| Role | Files | May import | Type-only import |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` | |
| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role | `api-app` |
| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` | |
| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` | |
| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role | |
| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` | |
| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role | |
| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` | `api-domain` |
| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` | |
| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role | |
| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` | |

Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
role.

The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
shows every role and every direction the rules allow, dashed where only a
type-only import is allowed. Each result has its own generated diagram,
[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
resolve to. Both come from `pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.

## Result structure

`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):

- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
  role.
- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
  rather than link it.
- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
  lists only external ones.
- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
  pragma.

## The api file roles

| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. Application calls it. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |

The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:

```ts
// apps/api/src/router.ts
import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
import { router } from './trpc.ts';

export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
```

Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
because Vite resolves it.

## The web state model

| State | Owner | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: effectTsResolver(schema), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
mutation or form of its own.

The api client is the only web module that names the api. Everything else
reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:

```ts
// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
const trpc = useTrpc();
const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));

// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const mutation = useMutation(
  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
  }),
);
```

Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:

```tsx
function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
  const view = render(
    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
      <GreetingPage />
    </TestApiProvider>,
  );
  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
}
```

A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

## The rules (and why)

Each rule fails a check on a seeded violation in a committed test
(`tooling/architecture/boundaries.test.ts`, `scripts/eslint-policy.test.ts`,
`tooling/architecture/typescript.test.ts`). The check's message names the fix.

| Rule | Why | Enforced by | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routes own page composition. | One place per page keeps navigation readable. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Sibling slices stand alone: a route imports no other route, a feature no other feature. | Each slice changes without breaking its siblings. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` for every result; Fallow child zones for `apps/web` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Every file belongs to one role and one slice. | Extra layers and loose files hide structure. | Fallow `coverage.requireAllFiles`; `policy/slice-isolation` for a loose file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm lint:policy` |
| A package reaches another only by its package name. | Public exports are the only contract. | `policy/slice-isolation` (relative import out of the package) | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| A module is imported through its `index.ts`. | The public surface is a deliberate, reviewed list. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports`; API reports | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm api:check` |
| Procedures validate their input with Effect Schema. | Data from the network is untrusted until parsed. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| Procedures delegate to application logic. | Transport stays thin; logic stays testable. | Fallow `api-procedures` value-imports only `api-trpc`, `api-application` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
| The domain is pure, and application knows no tRPC. | Rules test as plain functions. | Fallow `api-domain`; `contract/domain-pure`, `contract/application-without-trpc`; `tsconfig.domain.json` (no Node types) | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`, `pnpm typecheck` |
| Effects run only in integrations or the api composition root. | One place to swap storage or IO. | `contract/effects-in-integrations`, `contract/io-effects-in-integrations`, `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| The web reaches the api only through the api client and the router type. | The bundle carries no server code. | Fallow `allowTypeOnly`; the `types`-only export of `@repo/api`; `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client`, `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| UI primitives hold no business logic. | The kit stays reusable across results. | Fallow `ui` imports nothing; `contract/ui-without-logic` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| One React component per file. | One file, one reason to change. | ESLint `policy/one-component-per-file` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| State, server state and form state live in `use*` hooks. | Components render; hooks wire. | ESLint `policy/state-and-effects-in-hooks` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| Forms validate with Effect Schema. | One schema language across web and api. | ESLint `policy/form-uses-effect-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| Web code has the DOM and no Node; api code has no DOM and only erasable syntax; domain code has neither. | The browser has no Node, and Node strips types and runs the source as is. | `tsconfig.json` (web, ui), `tsconfig.api.json` and `tsconfig.domain.json` over `tsconfig.base.json` | `pnpm typecheck` |
| Behaviour is defined by each result's E2E specs. | The product contract survives refactors. | Playwright, one project per result | `pnpm e2e` |

`contract/<id>` is a rule in
[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc),
which Fallow loads as a rule pack and reports as an error. The behaviour map
is each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, for example
[`apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`](../../apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts); see
[ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-behaviour-mapped-with-e2e.md).

## Architecture checks

`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
file:

- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
  differs from a fresh run.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.

`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
included.

## Showcase results

A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.

- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
  nothing from another result.
- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.

## What this template intentionally omits

The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.

## How to extend

Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.

### Add an api feature

1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
   storage or any effect.
2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.

### Add a procedure

1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
   `.input(Schema.standardSchemaV1(schema))`.
2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
   delegate to one application function.
3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
   `procedures.test.ts`.

### Add a route

1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
   `index.ts` that exports the page.
2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
   runs every spec in that folder.

### Add a web feature

Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
import it through its `index.ts`.

### Finish

1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

check can decide; reviewers hold those. When in doubt, copy the reference

The Fallow rule pack

## Judgment calls

- **Full words in identifiers.** Write `name` and `request`. The name is the
  cheapest documentation an agent has. Established acronyms such as E2E, CI,
  ADR, UI, IO, and URL are fine.
- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See
  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.
- **Validate data at an IO boundary.** Parse network, storage, and environment
  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect
  Schema. A type assertion is a claim, and validation is proof.
- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.
- **Co-locate tests.** Each test sits beside its subject as `<Name>.test.ts(x)`.

# Definition of Done

A change is **done** when every box below is true. This is not aspirational —
the quality gates mechanically enforce most of it, so "done" and "passes the
gates" are the same statement. A task is not done until the changed behaviour is
verified by deterministic evidence: tests, build output, typecheck and lint
results, screenshots or video for user-visible behaviour, or another concrete
artifact that stands without anyone's judgment. An agent reports a task
complete once `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` are green.

## The checklist

- [ ] **Behaviour is specified.** New or changed behaviour is covered by a
      spec in the result's `web/e2e/` folder (the behaviour map), such as
      `apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`. The product's contract is explicit.
- [ ] **Logic is unit-tested.** Domain, application and procedures have `api`
      Jest tests; hooks and pages have `web` Jest tests that render through
      `TestApiProvider`. Coverage stays at/above the threshold in
      `jest.config.ts` (80%).
- [ ] **Types check.** `pnpm typecheck` passes its four programs,
      `tsconfig.json` (web and ui), `tsconfig.node.json` (configs and e2e),

## The one-command proof

```bash
pnpm verify   # typecheck → biome → eslint → fallow → architecture → unit tests → build → size
pnpm e2e      # every result's behaviour map + axe accessibility scan
```

If both are green and the checklist holds, the work is done. If either is red,
it is not — regardless of how finished the code looks.

## PR contract checks

The `PR quality` workflow runs
[`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`](../../scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs) on every
pull request event, including edits to the body. It fails the PR with a message
that names the fix unless:

- the body keeps the four [template](../../.github/pull_request_template.md)
  sections in order, each with real content: `Why does this feature exist?`,
  `What changed?`, `Behavioural Proof (with video and screenshots)`, and
  `Verification Summary`;
- the proof section embeds a screenshot inline with `![alt](url)`, or says
  `Not applicable` followed by the technical reason on the same line or the
  next one;
- every inline image is an absolute `https://` URL, and a GitHub blob URL ends
  in `?raw=1`, so the image renders;
- the proof section embeds its images instead of linking to them;
- the title is Conventional Commits, `type(scope): summary`, with no agent or
  tool prefix;
- the head branch is `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`;
- the Verification Summary has exactly one `- Head commit:` line naming one SHA
  (full or short) of the PR head, so a push that moves the head fails until the
  body is re-checked against it
  ([ADR 0029](../decisions/0029-pr-body-names-its-head-commit.md)).

## Proof judgment

These calls need a reviewer:

- Screenshots and video come from the branch under review and show the changed
  behaviour itself. Flows with motion or timing include video when practical.
- E2E tests map to the user-visible behaviour the PR changes.
- Every bug fix ships, in the same change, with the test that would have caught
  it. The test fails on the unfixed code and asserts the user-visible symptom.
- Missing visual proof or E2E coverage comes with a technical reason and the
  replacement verification method.
- Proof files live under `docs/proof/<short-scope>/` on the PR branch, unless
  the PR states a technical reason for another committed location. See
  [`.claude/skills/pr-inline-screenshot-proof/SKILL.md`](../../.claude/skills/pr-inline-screenshot-proof/SKILL.md).
- Each evidence link opens the rendered artifact once the branch is pushed.

## Verification

- Format, lint, typecheck, unit, integration, and E2E checks relevant to the
  changed files run after the final code change.
- The PR lists each command and its pass or fail result.
- The PR separates existing unrelated failures from failures it introduces.
- Each skipped check names its reason, risk, and follow-up owner.

The Todo result is built in `showcase/todo-01/`, and both gates pass: `pnpm verify` exits 0, and `pnpm e2e` passes all 22 tests. That includes the 7 fixed acceptance tests (`todo-01-acceptance`) and the result's own 8 specs. Coverage for this result is 100%. The work is uncommitted.

**Api (`@todo-01/api`)**
- The feature lives in `features/todos/` and follows the same file roles as the greeting feature: domain, application, integrations, procedures and index.
- Todos are kept in a `Map` in `integrations.ts`, inside the api process. Ids come from `randomUUID`.
- There are four procedures: `todos.list`, `todos.create`, `todos.toggle` and `todos.delete`. Each input is checked with Effect Schema. A blank title is rejected as a bad request, and toggling or deleting an id that doesn't exist returns "not found".

**Web (`@todo-01/web`)**
- The page is in `routes/todos/`, split into `TodosPage`, `TodoForm`, `TodoList` and `TodoItem`.
- Server data goes through `useTodos`, which uses TanStack Query over tRPC and refreshes the list after each change. The form goes through `useTodoForm`, which uses React Hook Form with the Effect Schema rules in `todoFormSchema`.
- Each todo's checkbox is a plain HTML checkbox, because `@repo/ui` has no checkbox and I could only write inside `showcase/todo-01/`. Everything else uses `Button` and `TextField` from `@repo/ui`.
- The api-client folder is copied from the reference. Only its import of the api package and its two tests changed, to point at `todos.list`.

Outside `showcase/`, the only change is `pnpm-lock.yaml`, which gained the two new packages.

**Behaviour to know about**
- The form clears as soon as you submit. If saving then fails, the page shows "Could not save the change" but the title you typed is gone.
- A checkbox changes only after the api confirms the toggle, not instantly on click.
